items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: So he said to his wife, 'Now, who am I going to get on bass, what bass player am I going to get?'

ctx.x: together and go to work. They called him for this thing with Maynard, called him to do the thing at the Tropicana. And his feelings were kind of similar to mine, that he didn't want to go to Las Vegas. He didn't want to work right then, he was off.

And Maynard talked him into it. So he said to his wife, 'Now, who am I going to get on bass, what bass player am I going to get?' And his wife said to him, 'Well, just get yourself some players and go up and make the job.' So he didn't know who to call. He was kind of...in his mind he didn't have a bass player to call. So he went to the union book and opened the union book, and when he just opened the union book to the bass players and looked, he said my name was right there.

He said he called his wife and said to her, 'Looka here. Why would Monk Montgomery's name come up? I don't know that man.' She said, 'Don't question it. Call him, just call him.' And when he called me, he even said it was urgent. And he talked to me as if he had to have me, and he followed through on that when he called me.

items.title: 56799_Red Norvo oral history interview
items.q: a Monk Montgomery who was with the Montgomery Brothers, was in San Francisco, so I hired him.

ctx.x: And I found at the other hotels it was the same way, so when I went in for Maynard, this little room in the Tropicana, we went in for three weeks. And I'd been working on -- oh, around the world with George Wean Williams, so I didn't really know men (unintelligible). Who was around. So I finally -- most the guys I wanted to get were busy or something. I remember a guitar clarinet player I'd heard in Phoenix, and a Monk Montgomery who was with the Montgomery Brothers, was in San Francisco, so I hired him. I said…
